report: Tiny green noise in dark scenes of a user-supplied 720x576 25 fps H.264 High (BT.601 limited, yuv420p) film under the balanced profile
path: software decode (hwdec no) -> vo=gpu OpenGL -> ARGB8888 4K draw surface on the VC4 overlay plane; DRM PRIME video plane disabled
method: Read-only dump of the scanout framebuffer through DRM GETFB2/PRIME while paused on dark frames, compared with a reference conversion of the same source frames. Runtime settings were changed only through the private player socket, then reset; temporary tools were removed from /tmp.
cause: Present in the source: near-black is encoded around Y 17-18 with U=V=129 (magenta-tinted black) and scattered lower chroma samples that decode to green-dominant pixels. The player reproduced them unfiltered, with bilinear 3.75x enlargement, dithering off and no deband. Framebuffer alpha was 255 everywhere and the conversion matched the reference, so overlay blending and colour-matrix errors were ruled out.
measure: Fraction of dark framebuffer pixels (max channel <= 24, pillarbox included) with G - max(R,B) >= 2

frame_4200.96s.after: not recorded: the post-change capture did not land on the same frame

installed_r7.contents: r5 controller/launcher/upload binaries byte-identical; new mpv.conf and dark-chroma.glsl. Only this package was signed; the other four APKs were carried over byte-for-byte.

follow_up: User still saw green specks on the TV with r7 at 4K output; they were gone at 1080p output. An offline simulation of the shader on 40 film frames left about 27 % of specks (9,712 -> 2,620). See cm5-20261115-output-mode.json.
